issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, the engine revving without the car speeding up, shuddering, or the SUV refusing to move in drive or reverse. Often around 90,000-100,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in these years wears internally, and transmission failure is the costliest and most common serious complaint for the 2001, 2006 and 2008 Tribute.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. If it is slipping or won't engage, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis. A rebuilt or used transmission is usually the fix, and costs vary a lot, so get more than one quote.

issues.sym: Check engine light (sometimes flashing), shaking at idle, stumbling under acceleration, especially in wet weather.
issues.why: The coil packs on the V6 fail with age and heat, and owners often replace several over time. A damaged wire between the fuel injectors and the engine computer can cause similar misfires. Misfires are the most reported problem on the Tribute.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to see which cylinder is affected. Replace the bad coil and spark plugs, and have the injector wiring checked if misfires keep coming back. Avoid long drives with a flashing check engine light, which can ruin the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Throttle body failure causes sudden power loss
issues.sym: The SUV suddenly loses power or goes into a low-power mode while driving, sometimes at highway speed, or stalls. A check engine or wrench light may come on.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body's motor and position sensor can wear out. When the engine computer can no longer trust the throttle signal it cuts power to protect the engine. This is a leading complaint for these years.
issues.next: Get safely off the road if it happens. Have the codes read and the throttle body tested; replacing it is the usual fix. Ask a Mazda dealer whether any extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Power steering assist can suddenly cut out (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, mainly at low speeds or when parking, often with a power steering warning on the dash.
issues.why: The torque sensor in the electric power steering can lose its signal, and the system then switches off power assist. Mazda recalled 2008-2011 Tributes to update software and replace faulty parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the steering goes heavy, you can still steer with more effort; slow down and get it to a dealer.

issues.t: Front lower control arm mount can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension over bumps, wandering steering, or in the worst case a front wheel moving out of position.
issues.why: In road-salt states, the body area where the front lower control arms attach can rust badly enough to separate, causing loss of steering control. Mazda recalled 2001-2004 Tributes to install a reinforcing brace.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the front subframe area inspected for rust before buying one.

issues.sym: The engine keeps revving or the SUV keeps accelerating after you lift off the gas, especially after pressing the pedal to the floor.
issues.why: On V6 models with cruise control, the cruise control cable connector could catch on the engine cover. Early models also had recalls for the cruise control servo and the accelerator cable not returning to idle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the throttle sticks, brake firmly and shift to neutral.

issues.t: ABS module connector can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: ABS warning light, smoke or a burning smell from the engine compartment, sometimes with the vehicle parked and off.
issues.why: Brake fluid could leak from the master cylinder cap onto the ABS module wiring connector, or missing seals let moisture in, causing corrosion, a short, and possibly a fire. Mazda issued two recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until it's fixed, park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Engine may stall when slowing down (recall)
issues.sym: The engine dies as you coast or brake to a stop.
issues.why: The engine computer programming on V6 models could let the idle drop too low while slowing down. Mazda recalled them to reprogram the computer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If stalls continue after the update, have the idle air control valve checked.

issues.t: Liftgate latch may open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal use.
issues.why: The rear liftgate latch did not meet federal strength rules and could open in a crash if left unlocked. Mazda recalled vehicles to replace the release rod, clip and handle spring.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Keep the liftgate locked while driving.

issues.sym: Play or looseness in the steering wheel.
issues.why: A cracked or badly assembled retaining nut could let the steering wheel loosen or separate. Mazda recalled early 2001 Tributes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Don't drive with a loose steering wheel.

issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drips near the fuel filter line.
issues.why: Damaged O-ring seals in a fuel line connector could leak fuel, creating a fire risk. Mazda recalled early 2001 Tributes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel, don't drive it until it's inspected.

issues.sym: The wipers stop moving or flop loosely while the motor still runs.
issues.why: A ball socket in the wiper linkage could break and disconnect the wipers. Mazda recalled vehicles to inspect and replace the wiper module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Pull over safely if the wipers stop in the rain.

issues.sym: Hybrid system warning lights, reduced power, or the SUV shutting down while driving.
issues.why: The electric pump that cools the hybrid electronics could fail, letting them overheat and shut down the powertrain. Mazda recalled 2008 Tribute Hybrids to fit an improved pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If hybrid warnings appear, have it checked before long drives.

issues.t: Shift lever can come loose on replacement transmissions (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the gear doesn't change, or the vehicle rolls after being put in Park.
issues.why: On 2008 Tributes fitted with a replacement transmission, the shift lever bolt could be under-tightened so the lever detaches. Mazda recalled them to tighten the bolt or replace the lever.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls, especially if the transmission was ever replaced. Always use the parking brake.

issues.t: Rust in the rear wheel wells and body
issues.sym: Bubbling paint and holes around the rear wheel openings and lower body, sometimes rusting all the way through.
issues.why: Salt and moisture collect in the wheel well lips and seams. Rusted-out wheel wells are the most reported single problem on the 2005 Tribute.
issues.next: Wash the underbody in winter and treat small rust early. Have badly rusted areas checked so structural parts aren't affected.

issues.sym: Cranks but won't start, or stalls and won't restart. You may not hear the pump hum when turning the key.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump, or its relay and fuse, wears out on these older Tributes. Owners report pump replacements on both the 4-cylinder and V6.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested and the pump relay and fuse checked before replacing the pump.

issues.sym: Sluggish acceleration, a rotten-egg smell, a check engine light, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Converters on the V6 can clog or fail, often after misfires have sent unburned fuel into them. Several owners report replacing more than one.
issues.next: Fix any misfire first, then have exhaust back-pressure tested. Replace the failed converter with one approved for your state.

issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out. On the V6 the pump is inside the engine and driven by the timing chain, so replacing it is a bigger job.
issues.next: Check the coolant level regularly and look for drips. Replace a leaking pump before the engine overheats.

issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with a rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: The EGR differential pressure feedback (DPFE) sensor that monitors exhaust gas recirculation tends to fail.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The sensor is inexpensive; replace its rubber hoses at the same time.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling from the idle air control valve
issues.sym: The idle surges or drops, or the engine stalls when cold or coming to a stop.
issues.why: The idle air control valve gets clogged or fails, and torn vacuum hoses can cause the same symptoms.
issues.next: Have the idle valve cleaned or replaced and the vacuum hoses checked for cracks.

issues.t: Ignition switch or lock module causes no-crank
issues.sym: Turning the key does nothing, or the key is hard to turn. The dash may light up but the engine won't crank.
issues.why: The ignition switch or ignition lock module can fail.
issues.next: Rule out a dead battery first. A shop can test the switch and the anti-theft key system.

issues.t: Check engine light or trouble after refueling
issues.sym: The pump keeps clicking off while filling, a check engine light appears after a fill-up, or the engine runs poorly right after refueling.
issues.why: Problems in the fuel filler neck, cap or evaporative emissions (EVAP) system, such as a failing canister vent, can cause these symptoms.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light stays on, have the EVAP system smoke-tested. Emissions parts may still be covered by your state's emissions warranty on hybrids.

issues.sym: The rear window suddenly breaks, sometimes when opening or closing the liftgate, with no impact.
issues.why: Owners report the rear glass shattering on its own, sometimes causing cuts. Stress at the glass hinges or latch can start the break.
issues.next: Open and close the glass gently and check the hinges for corrosion. Report any spontaneous breakage to NHTSA and the dealer.
